symbols.name: SYNTH_CONTEXT_BUDGET
doc: I set the per-circular context budget for the synthesis prompt. The route supplies the FULL circular text including multi-page annexures and tables. With Gemini Pro (2M token window) I allow up to 60,000 characters per circular, so full 10+ page circulars (e.g. Circular 3 higher education bond schedules) stay intact.

symbols.name: SYNTH_TOTAL_BUDGET
doc: ...but ALL the circulars together are capped as well (up to 5 sources). Real circulars average ~7.7k characters, so this rarely bites; it stops a worst case (5 x 60k = ~100k tokens, more for Hindi/Bengali) from blowing the 52 s deadline and the cost. The share per source is total / number of sources, never above SYNTH_CONTEXT_BUDGET; the numeric-priority condenser below trims a source that exceeds its share.

symbols.name: YEAR_RE
doc: SOURCE RELEVANCE PRE-FILTER This is a second, independent checkpoint layered on top of the existing search/qualification ranking in route.ts. I did not replace or touch that ranking (it stays untouched, for the same blast-radius reason as the earlier smartSemanticRouter.ts fix). The filter only removes candidates that ranking let through but that are DECISIVELY wrong on two specific, checkable axes, BEFORE they ever reach the LLM as context. They are not just hidden from the citation list afterward (that is the separate, already-shipped keyFindings-based filter further down in buildResult); this one is upstream of it, so a wrong source does not even get a chance to influence what the model writes.

1. YEAR MISMATCH: the query names an explicit year, and the candidate's own HEADLINE names a DIFFERENT explicit year. I deliberately check the HEADLINE's own stated year, not `publishedAt`'s calendar year: this corpus's holiday-list circulars are routinely published in December of the PRIOR year (the 2023 Holiday List circular is dated 26/12/2022), so comparing publishedAt's year directly would wrongly exclude the correct source. A circular whose own title says "-2025" answering a question about 2023 is unambiguously wrong regardless of when it was filed.

2. POPULATION MISMATCH: the query does not mention contract/contractor workers at all, but the candidate's headline is specifically about contract/contractor workers. They are a distinct, differently-administered population in this corpus (see the recurring "Holidays & Leaves for Contractor Workers" circulars), never the right source for an ordinary DSP-employee policy question.

Both checks are decisive (not scored/probabilistic) on purpose: this is exactly what was missing when "why is Maha Shivratri an extra holiday in 2023?" pulled in a 2025-dated Holiday List circular and two contractor-worker circulars at 88-90% match. Nothing upstream ever asked "does this source even claim to be about the right year and the right population," only "is this vector/lexically close enough." I kept it deliberately narrow: it does NOT attempt full topical/semantic relevance. A same-year, same-population but only tangentially related source (e.g. a generic Compensatory Off policy chunk) still passes this filter. Closing that gap is a much larger piece of work, intentionally left for a dedicated pass on the executive synthesis engine, not bundled into this fix.

symbols.name: ANNOUNCEMENT_BRIEF
symbols.sig: const ANNOUNCEMENT_BRIEF = `ANNOUNCEMENTS AMONG THE RECORDS: a record headed [Announcement id=...] is an announcement of the plant (a short notice, …
doc: I say this to the writer ONLY when an announcement is among the sources (a briefing made from circulars alone reads exactly what it always read, and its stored copies stay valid). Announcements are short notices of the plant, often bound to a period, so the rules are about dates and about never presenting an old notice as current.

symbols.name: announcementFingerprint
doc: This is the part of a stored briefing's validity that the circulars' fingerprint cannot know: WHICH announcements it was made from and what they said. It is empty when there is none (a briefing from circulars alone is unchanged).

symbols.name: PROMPT_SIG
doc: A short signature of the prompt. It is part of the key of a stored briefing, so a changed prompt can never serve a briefing made with the old one.

symbols.name: EDS_ENGINE_VERSION
doc: ONE BRIEFING PER QUESTION: stored, scored, consistent. I make a question's briefing ONCE and then read it back:
1. this server's memory (valid while the archive of circulars is unchanged),
2. the permanent store (edsStore.ts, table eds_briefing): any server, any day, until the archive or the engine changes,

3. otherwise it is MADE: several candidates are written at once, each is scored by plain code (edsQuality.ts), the best one is kept, and, if it is good enough, written to the store. Two servers making the same question together both end up showing the row that was stored first.

A question typed with other capitals, spaces or punctuation is the same question. A question worded differently is a different question. If the model cannot be reached (no credit, outage), I show a briefing stored for an older archive rather than nothing.
Change this when the scoring or the chart/table rules change: every stored briefing made under the old rules is then made afresh.

symbols.name: EDS_DEADLINE_MS
doc: The whole making of one briefing (writing, checking, storing) must end within this, which is under the route's maxDuration (120 s, src/app/api/ai-search/route.ts).

symbols.name: VERIFY_MIN_MS
doc: I attempt the second reading only when at least this much of the deadline is left

symbols.name: isRangeLabel
symbols.sig: export function isRangeLabel(label: string | undefined): boolean
doc: The chart type is a rule of the DATA, not a choice of the model: the same numbers must be drawn the same way at every ask (before, one run called "4x and 2x" a breakdown and drew a pie, the next called it a comparison and drew columns).
- a pie only for parts of ONE whole: the intent says breakdown, the unit is not a multiple / rate / ratio / duration, one series, 2 or more parts;
- two series (a second value on the items) are columns, whatever the intent said;
- a pie that fails those tests is columns (one series).
A label that spans a period ("MAR-25 TO AUG-25", "Jan - Mar", "2022 \u2013 2024") counts as a range, not one moment.

doc: Builds the comparison table, and I apply three sparsity guards here:
(a) drop any comparison column (index >= 1) whose every body cell is empty;
(b) drop rows left with no informative value after (a);
(c) drop the whole table if it is still mostly empty (< 40% informative body cells), because a wall of "Not stated" is noise and the overview already states the gap.

symbols.name: isEmptyCell
doc: A cell / finding that conveys no information: "Not stated in circular", "N/A", "-", "—", "not available", empty, etc.

symbols.name: isNonFinding
doc: A "finding" that is really just a statement of absence, e.g. "Number of awards per month: not stated in circular". Unlike a table cell, the non-informative phrase can sit anywhere in the sentence (often after a colon), so I scan the whole text rather than only its start.

symbols.name: NUMBER_WORDS
symbols.sig: const NUMBER_WORDS: Record<string, string> = { once: "1", twice: "2", thrice: "3", one: "1", two: "2", three: "3", four: "4", five: "5", six: "6", seven: "7", eight: …
doc: ONE written form for a value cell of the comparison table, whatever words the model chose: "<rate> (<authority>) [<condition>]". "Four times of the base rate (Auth: Head of Dept)" -> "4x base rate (Head of Dept)" "Twice of the base rate" -> "2x base rate" The screen draws the rate in bold, the authority as a chip and the condition as a note, and reads exactly this form.

doc: The first date that a timeline label names ("31.10.2023", "28.12.2023 to 30.12.2023", "5th December, 2024", "Dec 2024", "2024-12-05"), as a sortable number; null when it names none.

symbols.name: chronologicalOrder
symbols.sig: export function chronologicalOrder<T extends { label: string }>(items: T[]): T[]
doc: A timeline is in the order of time: when EVERY point names a date, I sort them by it (the model sometimes lists a deadline after the start it precedes). Otherwise the order given stands.

symbols.name: MONTH_NUMBER
symbols.sig: const MONTH_NUMBER: Record<string, number> = { jan: 1, feb: 2, mar: 3, apr: 4, may: 5, jun: 6, jul: 7, aug: 8, sep: 9, oct: 10, nov: 11, dec: 12 }
doc: ---- dates: a date is grounded by WHAT date it is, not by how it is written ----

The circular writes "31st December'2023"; the briefing writes "31.12.2023". Compared as numbers ("31.12", "2023") the second looked invented and the finding holding it was thrown away. Here I read both to day-month-year, and a numeric date in the briefing that the circulars write in ANY form is not checked digit by digit. A date the circulars do not contain is still checked like any figure (and fails).

symbols.name: figureGuard
symbols.sig: export function figureGuard(sourceText: string, labels?: Map<number, string>): { numberIsGrounded: (n: number) => boolean; figuresSafe: (text: string) => boolean; sourceDates: Set<string>; percentsSafe: (text: string) => boolean }
symbols.returns: { numberIsGrounded: (n: number) => boolean; figuresSafe: (text: string) => boolean; sourceDates: Set<string>; percentsSafe: (text: string) => boolean }
doc: The figure guard of a set of circulars: `numberIsGrounded(n)` is true when the number is written in them, `figuresSafe(text)` when every substantial number of the text is. buildResult uses it on the writer's output, and the verifier's repairs (edsVerify.ts) use it alike. Small whole numbers (3..31: a multiplier, a month, a count) must be WRITTEN in the circulars too, as digits or as a word ("Four times", "Twice", "sixth"); 0, 1 and 2 stay free ("Standard HRR" is 1x; "two sides"). The archive's own name for a circular ("Circular 007 (2026)") has numbers in it that are the archive's, not claims, and a date the circulars write is not a figure: I check neither.

symbols.name: percentFiguresIn
doc: The numbers a text writes AS A PERCENTAGE ("25%", "25 %", "25 per cent", "7.5 percent"). A percentage in a briefing must be printed as a percentage in the circulars: "all contributions are exempt" is not "100% exempt", and a bare 100 that happens to stand elsewhere (a Rs 100 fee, a clause number) does not make it so.

symbols.name: normalizeNum
doc: I normalize a number to a canonical key so 20995.30, 20995.3, "20,995.30" and "20995.300" all compare equal. I keep up to 2 decimals (rupee paise).

symbols.name: extractGroundedNumbers
doc: All numbers literally present in the source text, returned as a Set of normalized keys.

symbols.name: extractNumbersFromText
doc: Extracts the substantial numbers from a piece of model text (same thousands-separator handling), for the grounding checks.

symbols.name: groundTable
symbols.sig: function groundTable( table: SynthesisTable, ok: (n: number) => boolean, clean: (cell: string) => string = (c) => c, textOk: (cell: string) => boolean = () => true,): SynthesisTable | null
doc: Drops the table rows whose value cells contain an ungrounded number. A cell that is text-only (e.g. "Discontinued") is kept. If a value column ends up all empty, buildTable's caller already handled emptiness; here I re-run the emptiness guard after grounding.

symbols.name: groundChart
